```json
  [
      {
        fieldName: "name",
        fieldType: "String",
        filterType: "contains",
        filterValue: "a"
      }
  ]
```

The operator used between the different conditions passed will be **AND**, so the returned entities must fulfill all the conditions sent in the filters array. Also, the same field can be sent multiple times if for example you want to filter for names that start with A and also contain XY.

For the `fieldName` property, you should send it formatted as it follows:
- If it is a default attribute, send just the name: `name`, `size`, `created_at`, `owners_csm`, etc
- If it is a custom attribute, send it using dot-notation, as follows: `custom_attributes.myAttribute`, `custom_attributes.deal_stage`, etc
- If you want to filter by tag, sent the name `tags`
- If you want to filter by a calculated metric, sent it as `metrics.calculated_metrics.CALCULATED_METRIC_ID`, example `metrics.calculated_metrics.5fa5b24f584088153f7fd825`
- If you want to filter by a health score, send it as `metrics.health_scores.HEALTH_SCORE_ID`, example `metrics.health_scores.5f86fee26e8f7c489b28dd03`

Possible values for `fieldType`, with associated values for the other properties as well:
- **Number**:
    - Available for all numerical default and custom attributes as well as calculated metrics and health scores and has the following possible `filterType` values:
        - `greater` - the value of the attribute/metric is greater than the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `lower` - the value of the attribute/metric is lower than the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `is` - the value of the attribute/metric is equal to the value provided in the `filterValue` field

        - `is_unknown` - the attribute/metric does not exist on the entity. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string

        - `is_average` - the health score is average, meaning the value of the health score is in the orange area as defined in the health score settings
        - `is_good` - the health score is good, meaning the value of the health score is in the green area as defined in the health score settings

        - `is_not` - the value of the attribute is different from the value provided in the `filterValue` field

In the body of the request you can send the CSAT score (`score`), a comment (`comment`) and the date of the CSAT score (`submittedAt`). Only the field `score` is required. If you don't provide the `submittedAt` field it will be saved the current UTC time.
If the people for which you're sending the CSAT score already has saved a CSAT score, it will be kept the newest one based on the `submittedAt` date field.
If the people you're assigning the CSAT score is linked to a company then also the company gets assigned a CSAT score which is calculated as the arithmetic mean (rounded to the nearest integer) of all people's CSAT scores that are linked to the company.

### Filtering notes
If you want to apply filters to this endpoint, you would need to send the `filters` query parameter as an URL-encoded array of objects as follows:
```json
[
  {
    field: "createdByEntity", //the field to filter by
    values: ['629dfbc3e827ed3cd0de1a53',…] //the values
  },
  ...
]
```
The logic applied to filtering is `OR` between different values for the same field and `AND` between different fields, for example:
```
(createdByEntity='value1' OR createdByEntity='value2') AND (tags='value3' OR tags='value4')
```

The following fields can be filtered (including what can be sent in the values array):
  - `createdByEntity` - filters notes by who/what they were created by. The allowed values are `api`, `playbook_{id}`, `user_{id}`, `integration_{id}` where `{id}` is the Custify ID of the entity (for playbook and user) 
or the name of the integration (like `hubspot`, `close`) that have created the note
  - `tags` - filters notes by tags, the values being Custify IDs of Tags
  - `mentioning` - filters notes by users mentioned in them, the values being Custify IDs of users

Extra filtering can be archived by using the `searchTerm` query parameter and should be a string. This will filter notes by the text they contain or by the external ID if the note came from a integration.

data.current_summary: Assign a nps score to a people
data.current_description:
You can assign a nps score to a people by sending a POST request to [https://api.custify.com/nps_score/{entity}](https://api.custify.com/nps_score/{entity}), where {entity} is the Custify internal `id` of the People.
Alternatively, you can assign a nps score to a people by sending a POST request to:
- [https://api.custify.com/nps_score?email=john.doe@custify.com](https://api.custify.com/nps_score?email=john.doe@custify.com) or
- [https://api.custify.com/nps_score?user_id=123](https://api.custify.com/nps_score?user_id=123) where `user_id` is the ID from your system.
You can also assign the nps score to a survey by sending a POST request to [https://api.custify.com/nps_score?{surveyId=xyz}](https://api.custify.com/nps_score?{surveyId=xyz}), where {surveyId} is the Custify internal `id` of the Survey.

In the body of the request you can send the NPS score (`score`), a comment (`comment`) and the date of the NPS score (`submittedAt`). Only the field `score` is required. If you don't provide the `submittedAt` field it will be saved the current UTC time.
If the people for which you're sending the NPS score already has saved a NPS score, it will be kept the newest one based on the `submittedAt` date field.
If the people you're assigning the NPS score is linked to a company then also the company gets assigned a NPS score which is calculated as the arithmetic mean (rounded to the nearest integer) of all people's NPS scores that are linked to the company.

You can send batch requests for creating/updating people or companies, for creating events or custom data. The requests can be processes synchronous or asynchronous based on the value sent in the request. The default processing is asynchronous.
For asynchronous jobs you can have a return job id which can be used to retrieve the status of the processing. If synchronous is set to true then the maximum number of jobs you can provide is 3. If synchronous is set to false you can provide maximum 100 jobs.
The jobs can be mixed (for people, companies, events or custom data). The return job id is kept for 6 hours after the last job in the batch is processed. The payload of the job depends of the type of job and should contain data in the same format as when creating/updating people, companies or events.
For custom data the payload should look like:
```json
{
  "type": "custom-data",
  "payload": {
    "entity": "65240f85e2a675bd3090a3d3",
    "entityModel": "Company",
    "data_type": "invoice",
    "data_id": "INV_003",
    "data": {
        "amount": 175,
        "invoiced_at": "2023-02-02T00:00:00Z",
        "is_paid": false,
        "product_name": "bronze_plan"
    }
  }
}
```
Alternatively, if you don't know the Custify entity ID you can send the `company_id` or `user_id` from your system by replacing field `entity` in the payload.

data.current_description:
You can fetch a list of companies. The list, by default, is sorted by the `signed_up_at` field and in `descending` order, with the most recent signups first.
### Filtering companies
If you want to apply filters to the `/company/all` endpoint, you would need to send the `filters` query parameter as an URL-encoded array of objects as follows:
```json
  [
      {
        fieldName: "name",
        fieldType: "String",
        filterType: "contains",
        filterValue: "a"
      }
  ]
```

The operator used between the different conditions passed will be **AND**, so the returned entities must fulfill all the conditions sent in the filters array. Also, the same field can be sent multiple times if for example you want to filter for names that start with A and also contain XY.

For the `fieldName` property, you should send it formatted as it follows:
- If it is a default attribute, send just the name: `name`, `size`, `created_at`, `owners_csm`, etc
- If it is a custom attribute, send it using dot-notation, as follows: `custom_attributes.myAttribute`, `custom_attributes.deal_stage`, etc
- If you want to filter by tag, sent the name `tags`
- If you want to filter by a calculated metric, sent it as `metrics.calculated_metrics.CALCULATED_METRIC_ID`, example `metrics.calculated_metrics.5fa5b24f584088153f7fd825`
- If you want to filter by a health score, send it as `metrics.health_scores.HEALTH_SCORE_ID`, example `metrics.health_scores.5f86fee26e8f7c489b28dd03`

Possible values for `fieldType`, with associated values for the other properties as well:
- **Number**:
    - Available for all numerical default and custom attributes as well as calculated metrics and health scores and has the following possible `filterType` values:
        - `greater` - the value of the attribute/metric is greater than the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `lower` - the value of the attribute/metric is lower than the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `is` - the value of the attribute/metric is equal to the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `is_not` - the value of the attribute/metric is different from the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `is_unknown` - the attribute/metric does not exist on the entity. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string
        - `any_value` - the attribute/metric exists on the entity and has any value. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string
    - If the `fieldName` is a health score, there are 3 additional `filterType` options that can be used. For all of them the `filterValue` should be either an empty string or NULL:
        - `is_bad` - the health score is bad, meaning the value of the health score is in the red area as defined in the health score settings
        - `is_average` - the health score is average, meaning the value of the health score is in the orange area as defined in the health score settings
        - `is_good` - the health score is good, meaning the value of the health score is in the green area as defined in the health score settings
- **String**:
    - Available for all textual default and custom attributes and has the following possible `filterType` values:
        - `is` - the value of the attribute is equal to the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `is_not` - the value of the attribute is different from the value provided in the `filterValue` field
        - `starts_with` - the value of the attribute starts with the value provided in `filterValue`
        - `ends_with` - the value of the attribute ends with the value provided in `filterValue`
        - `contains` - the value of the attribute contains the value provided in `filterValue`
        - `does_not_contain` - the value of the attribute does not contain the value provided in `filterValue`
        - `is_unknown` - the attribute/metric does not exist on the entity. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string
        - `any_value` - the attribute/metric exists on the entity and has any value. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string
    - Should also be used when the `fieldName` is `owners_csm` or `owners_account` (when filtering by Company CSM or Company Account Manager), but then the possible `filterType` values are:
        - `is` - in this particular case the `filterValue` should contain the Custify User ID of the CSM / Account Manager
        - `is_unknown` - means that the company does not have a CSM / Account Manager
- **User**:
    - Available for attributes of type `User` (created using Event-attribute editor) and has the following possible `filterType` values:
        - `is` - the value of the attribute is equal to the value provided in the `filterValue` field and should contain the Custify User ID of the user
        - `is_unknown` - the attribute does not exist on the entity. The `filterValue` can be sent as either NULL or empty string
- **Date**:
    - Available for all date default and custom attributes and has the following possible values for `filterType`:
        - `more_than` - means that the value of the attribute is more than X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` - which is a Number) days ago
        - `exactly` - means that the value of the attribute is exactly X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` - which is a Number) days ago
        - `less_than` - means that the value of the attribute is less than X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` - which is a Number) days ago
        - `after` - means that the value of the attribute is after the date X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format)
        - `on`  - means that the value of the attribute is on the date X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format)
        - `before`  - means that the value of the attribute is before the date X (where X is the value provided in `filterValue` in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format)
        - `between`  - means that the value of the attribute is between the dates X and Y (where X and Y are the value provided in `filterValue` as an array `[X,Y]` each in the `YYYY-MM-DD` format)
- **Boolean**:
    - Available for all boolean default and custom attributes and has the following possible values for `filterType`. Also, for Boolean fields the `filterValue` should always be empty string or NULL:
        - `true` - the value of the attribute is TRUE
        - `false` - the value of the attribute is FALSE
        - `is_unknown` - the attribute does not exist on the entity
        - `any_value` - the attribute exists on the entity and has any value
- **Tag**:
    - This is the `fieldType` that must be used when filtering for the `tags` field and the following options for `filterType` are available
        - `is_in` - the `filterValue` must be the Custify ID of a tag and will return entities that have that tag applied
        - `is_not_in` - the `filterValue` must be the Custify ID of a tag and will return entities that do not have that tag applied
        - `is_unknown` - the `filterValue` should be either NULL or an empty string and will return entities that have no tags applied to them
- **Company**:
    - This is the `fieldType` that must be used when filtering on `People` to retrieve people that are part of the specified company. The following options for `filterType` are available
        - `is_in` - the `filterValue` must be the Custify ID of a company and will return entities that match the applied filter
        - `is_unknown` - the `filterValue` should be either NULL or an empty string and will return entities that match the applied filter

Filtering for `Parent companies` can be done using the following values for the fields:
- `fieldName` should be `parent_companies`
- `fieldType` should be `String`
- `filterType` should have one of the options:
    - `is_descendant` - will return entities that are descendants (children, grand-children, etc...) of the company set in the `filterValue` field
    - `is_in` - will return entities that are children of the company set in the `filterValue` field
- `filterValue` should be the Custify internal ID of the company for which the filtering values is applied.
### Filtering properties
If you want to apply filters to the response from `/company/all` endpoint, you would need to send the `properties` query parameter as an URL-encoded array of fields to be returned.
Some default properties are available for all entities: `id`, `name`, `created_at` and `updated_at`.

data.current_summary: Assign a CSAT score to a people
data.current_description:
You can assign a CSAT score to a people by sending a POST request to [https://api.custify.com/csat_score/{entity}](https://api.custify.com/csat_score/{entity}), where {entity} is the Custify internal `id` of the People.
Alternatively, you can assign a CSAT score to a people by sending a POST request to:
- [https://api.custify.com/csat_score?email=john.doe@custify.com](https://api.custify.com/csat_score?email=john.doe@custify.com) or
- [https://api.custify.com/csat_score?user_id=123](https://api.custify.com/csat_score?user_id=123) where `user_id` is the ID from your system.
You can also assign the CSAT score to a survey by sending a POST request to [https://api.custify.com/csat_score?{surveyId=xyz}](https://api.custify.com/csat_score?{surveyId=xyz}), where {surveyId} is the Custify internal `id` of the Survey.

In the body of the request you can send the CSAT score (`score`), a comment (`comment`) and the date of the CSAT score (`submittedAt`). Only the field `score` is required. If you don't provide the `submittedAt` field it will be saved the current UTC time.
If the people for which you're sending the CSAT score already has saved a CSAT score, it will be kept the newest one based on the `submittedAt` date field.
If the people you're assigning the CSAT score is linked to a company then also the company gets assigned a CSAT score which is calculated as the arithmetic mean (rounded to the nearest integer) of all people's CSAT scores that are linked to the company.

Request body requires `score` (required), and optionally `comment` and `submittedAt` (defaults to current UTC time). If person already has a CSAT score, the newer one (by `submittedAt` date) is retained. Side effect: If the person is linked to a company, the company's CSAT score is automatically recalculated as the arithmetic mean of all linked people's scores. Returns the recorded CSAT score object.
